title: Fuse and E-Stop Power Path
creator: Dan McCreary
subject: Electronics for Robotics
description: A 12 V supply, a fuse, an E-stop contact and an arm motor board in series. Predict whether the arm runs, the fuse blows, or the E-stop stops the arm in six situations, watch the current dots stop, then explore your own fuse, load and E-stop settings. Used in Chapter 3.

educational.topic: Fuses and hardware emergency stops in a power path
learningObjectives: Infer whether a robot arm keeps running, loses power through its E-stop, or loses power because its fuse blows, in six situations, with at least 5 of 6 correct on the first attempt

pedagogical.teachingStrategy: Predict or set a value first, then watch animated current confirm or correct it
keyQuestions: Why does the fuse survive when the E-stop is pressed?
What would a bigger fuse do to the wires in a short circuit?
commonMisconceptions: A fuse blows whenever current flows
An E-stop button can blow the fuse
A larger fuse is always safer
assessmentOpportunities: Six committed predictions; 5 of 6 for mastery
